label: rem:vdw-pskew-isolation-interpretation
title: Van der Waals is the discarded sinh residual, the same Hopf channel as $\alpha_{EM}$
html:
Van der Waals is the bar-odd residual \sinh(2\lambda)\,(e_+-e_-). The \sinh channel represents the antisymmetric Coulomb–EM channel. The canonical P_{\mathrm{avg}} projection discards it. This explains why the van der Waals force remains small (a discarded residual), suppressed by \sinh rather than carrying covalent-scale energy, and absent from the main mass formula. The retained bar-even part acts exclusively as the trivial \cosh(2\lambda)\,\mathbf 1 carrier (the "hidden cosh"). This retained part is not itself the van der Waals energy.

Im(q) caveat. The P_{\mathrm{skew}} (\sinh) content acts entirely real at real q. It is kept then discarded, not imaginary. \mathrm{Im}(q) acts as a completely separate lever, formally set to zero by convention. The van der Waals residual operates as a real observable residing strictly in the discarded sector. A non-zero \mathrm{Im}(q) initiates a distinct, later refinement, safely separate from this channel.

\alpha_{EM} occupies the same Hopf channel. The fine-structure constant acts as a 2-strand Hopf-operation coupling. The 2-strand braiding harbors exactly the two idempotents e_+, e_-. Combining prior uniqueness rules establishes \alpha_{EM} as the unique multiple of the antisymmetric e_- coupling: \alpha_{EM} = h^2/(q\,\delta_q(T_{2,9})\delta_q(T_{3,5})), with \delta_q(T_{2,k}) = q^k - q^{-k} = h\,[k]_q representing the \sinh trace. Consequently, \alpha_{EM} (the e_- coupling) and the van der Waals force (the bar-odd \sinh residual) identically construct the same antisymmetric \sinh/EM channel of the Hopf operation. The fine-structure constant and the dispersion force formally represent two faces of a single Hopf knot operation. The \alpha_{EM} Habiro element H = [2]_q(1-h^2\alpha) = 2\cosh\lambda\,(1-h^2\alpha) constitutes the bar-even next-order correction, positioned opposite the bar-odd van der Waals term.

At q_0: \cosh(2\lambda) \approx 1.0219. The bar-odd residual evaluates exactly to \sinh(2\lambda)(e_+-e_-) \approx 0.10624 without fitting.

The molecular van der Waals energy emerges as the archimedean projection of the exact bar-odd expression. It is not an h^k fit or a \cosh factor on the covalent ladder. The single remaining open piece involves the archimedean inter-molecular separation (1/r^6). This spatial term scales the exact fibre residual to the observed molecular energy, remaining strictly open.
